records.source: וַ֭יַּעַן בִּלְדַּ֥ד הַשּׁוּחִ֗י וַיֹאמַֽר׃
records.gloss: And answered Bildad the Shuhite and said:
pieces: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered:

L.1: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:

decisions.choice: Bildad the Shuhite: the second of Job's three friends
decisions.reason: Bildad was introduced in 2:11. "Shuhite" names his people or home; Shuah is the name of a son of Abraham and Keturah whose descendants lived in the east (Genesis 25:2, 6). Where the place was is not known.

decisions.choice: answered and said: the usual opening of a speech
decisions.reason: "He answered and said" introduces each speech in the dialogue (4:1; 6:1). Bildad answers Job's words in chapters 6 and 7.

decisions.choice: answered (Balanced), said (Readable), without "and said"
decisions.reason: Hebrew introduces speech with two verbs, "answered and said". Literal keeps both; Balanced and Readable say it once, with the same wording at every speech introduction in Job.

records.heading: Bildad: does God twist justice?

records.source: עַד־אָ֥ן תְּמַלֶּל־אֵ֑לֶּה וְר֥וּחַ כַּ֝בִּיר אִמְרֵי־פִֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Until when will you speak these [things], and a mighty wind [are] the words of your mouth?
pieces: How long will you go on talking like this? \q Your words are a blustering wind.

L.2: How long will you speak these [things], \q and the words of your mouth [be] a mighty wind?

R.2: How long will you keep talking like this? \q Your words are nothing but a lot of wind.

decisions.choice: how long: an impatient question
decisions.reason: "Until when" ('ad 'an) asks how long something will go on, with the sense that it has gone on too long (18:2; 19:2).

decisions.choice: a mighty wind: words that are loud but empty
decisions.reason: Wind is a picture of words without substance (15:2; 16:3). Job had said his friends treat a desperate man's words as wind (6:26); Bildad does just that.

decisions.choice: the second half is part of the question
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the second line with "and", so the question may cover both: "How long will ... the words of your mouth be a mighty wind?" The sense is the same either way: Job's words are bluster.

decisions.choice: a statement in the second line
alternatives: How long will your words be a strong wind?
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the second line a statement, which says the same as the question in plainer English (m3).

records.source: הַ֭אֵל יְעַוֵּ֣ת מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וְאִם־שַׁ֝דַּ֗י יְעַוֵּֽת־צֶֽדֶק׃
records.gloss: Does God pervert justice, or does the Almighty pervert righteousness?
pieces: Does God twist justice? \q Does the Almighty twist what is right?

L.3: Does God pervert justice, \q or does the Almighty pervert righteousness?

R.3: Does God ever twist justice? \q Would God All-Powerful make wrong what is right?

decisions.choice: justice and righteousness: what is right and fair
decisions.reason: Justice (mishpat) is right judgment; righteousness (tsedeq) is what is right. Bildad sets the question at the heart of the book: if God is just, Job's suffering must be deserved. He answers Job's complaint that he is treated unjustly (6:29-30; 7:20).

decisions.choice: pervert: bend, make crooked
decisions.reason: The verb ('iwwet) means to bend or twist what is straight (Ecclesiastes 7:13; Lamentations 3:36). Elihu says the same in 34:12. The repeated verb gives the line its force.

decisions.choice: God and the Almighty
decisions.reason: 'El is "God"; Shaddai is "the Almighty", a name of God used often in Job (5:17; 6:4).

decisions.choice: God All-Powerful
decisions.reason: Readable says "God All-Powerful" for Shaddai, the book's choice, so the name is clear to new readers.

records.source: אִם־בָּנֶ֥יךָ חָֽטְאוּ־ל֑וֹ וַֽ֝יְשַׁלְּחֵ֗ם בְּיַד־פִּשְׁעָֽם׃
records.gloss: If your sons sinned against him, then he sent them into [the] hand of their transgression.
pieces: If your children sinned against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} handed them over to the power of their own wrongdoing.

L.4: If your children sinned against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent them away into the hand of their transgression.

R.4: If your children sinned against God, \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let them suffer the results of their own wrongdoing.

decisions.choice: your children: their death in 1:18-19
decisions.reason: Job's sons and daughters died when the house fell on them (1:18-19). Bildad draws the harsh conclusion that they must have sinned and been punished. The reader knows from 1:5 that Job used to offer sacrifices in case they had sinned.

decisions.choice: sent them into the hand of their transgression: gave them over to its results
decisions.reason: "Into the hand of" means into the power of. Their own wrongdoing became the thing that destroyed them (compare Proverbs 5:22).

decisions.choice: if: put as a condition, but meant as a judgment
decisions.reason: Bildad says "if", but he speaks as though the case is clear: their death proves their sin.

decisions.choice: children: sons, and here sons and daughters
decisions.reason: The word is "sons" (banim), but Job lost both sons and daughters (1:2, 18-19), and the plural can include both.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God, since "him" after "your children" could be misread.

records.source: אִם־אַ֭תָּה תְּשַׁחֵ֣ר אֶל־אֵ֑ל וְאֶל־שַׁ֝דַּ֗י תִּתְחַנָּֽן׃
records.gloss: If you will seek earnestly to God and to the Almighty plead for favor,
pieces: But if you will seek God earnestly \q and plead with the Almighty for mercy,

L.5: If you will seek God earnestly \q and plead for mercy with the Almighty,

R.5: But if you will look to God with all your heart \q and beg God All-Powerful for mercy,

decisions.choice: seek earnestly: the verb Job used in 7:21
decisions.reason: The verb (shachar) is the one Job used when he said God would look for him and he would be gone (7:21). Bildad turns it round: it is Job who must look for God.

decisions.choice: plead for mercy: ask for favor
decisions.reason: The verb (hitchannen) means to ask for grace or favor (Deuteronomy 3:23; Esther 4:8). Job uses it of himself in 9:15.

decisions.choice: you: set against your children
decisions.reason: The pronoun "you" is written out, which makes it emphatic: Job's children are gone, but Job himself may still turn to God. The sentence runs on through verses 6 and 7.

decisions.choice: But if
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "But" to show the contrast with verse 4 (m3).

decisions.choice: God ... God All-Powerful
decisions.reason: Readable says "God All-Powerful" for Shaddai, the book's choice.

records.source: אִם־זַ֥ךְ וְיָשָׁ֗ר אָ֥תָּה כִּי־עַ֭תָּה יָעִ֣יר עָלֶ֑יךָ וְ֝שִׁלַּ֗ם נְוַ֣ת צִדְקֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: If pure and upright you [are], surely now he will awake over you and restore [the] dwelling of your righteousness.
pieces: if you are pure and upright, \q then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise up for you at once \q and restore your rightful home.

L.6: if you [are] pure and upright, \q surely now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rouse {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} for you \q and restore the dwelling of your righteousness.

R.6: if you are pure and do what is right, \q God will act for you right away \q and give back the home that is rightly yours.

decisions.choice: pure and upright: clean of wrongdoing and straight in conduct
decisions.reason: Pure (zakh) means clean, without fault (11:4; 33:9); upright (yashar) is the word used of Job in 1:1. Bildad's "if" suggests he doubts it.

decisions.choice: rouse himself for you: act for you
decisions.reason: "Wake up over you" is a picture of God rising to act, as in the psalms (Psalm 7:7; 35:23). Here it is for Job's good.

decisions.choice: the dwelling of your righteousness: the home that is yours by right
decisions.reason: The dwelling (nawah) is a home or pasture-ground. "Of your righteousness" may mean the home a righteous man deserves, or the home where he lives rightly; either way God will give back Job's house and household.

decisions.choice: surely now: at once
decisions.reason: "For now" (ki 'attah) here means that God will act without delay.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God, since a sentence this long would leave "he" unclear.

records.source: וְהָיָ֣ה רֵאשִׁיתְךָ֣ מִצְעָ֑ר וְ֝אַחֲרִיתְךָ֗ יִשְׂגֶּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And will be your beginning small, and your end will grow very great.
pieces: Though your beginning was small, \q your future will be very great.

L.7: And your beginning will be small, \q but your latter end will grow very great.

R.7: What you had before will seem small \q compared with what you will have in the future.

decisions.choice: beginning and latter end: his earlier and his later state
decisions.reason: The beginning (re'shit) is what Job had before; the latter end ('acharit) is his future. The same word is used in 42:12, where the LORD blesses "the latter end of Job" more than his beginning: Bildad's words come true, though not for his reasons.

decisions.choice: small beside great: a comparison
decisions.reason: The two lines compare: what Job had will look small next to what he will have.

decisions.choice: grow: increase
decisions.reason: The verb (sagah) means to grow large; it is used of the reed growing in 8:11.

decisions.choice: a comparison clause
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable shape the two lines as a comparison (m2), since "your beginning will be small" would sound like a prophecy that Job's start will be poor.

records.source: כִּֽי־שְׁאַל־נָ֭א לְדֹ֣ר רִישׁ֑וֹן וְ֝כוֹנֵ֗ן לְחֵ֣קֶר אֲבוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: For ask, please, of [the] former generation, and apply [yourself] to the searching out of their fathers.
pieces: Ask the generation that went before, \q and consider what their ancestors discovered.

L.8: For ask, please, of [the] former generation, \q and give attention to what their fathers searched out.

R.8: Ask the people of earlier times. \q Think about what their ancestors learned.

decisions.choice: ask the former generation: the wisdom handed down
decisions.reason: Bildad appeals to the wisdom of the past, passed from father to son (15:18; Deuteronomy 32:7). A single life is too short to learn it alone (8:9).

decisions.choice: searching out: what was found by long inquiry
decisions.reason: The word (cheqer) means a searching, and what such searching discovers (5:27; 28:27).

decisions.choice: give attention: set your mind on
decisions.reason: The verb (konen) means to set firm; here, to set one's mind on something, to consider it carefully.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: "Fathers" ('avot) here means forebears; Balanced and Readable say "ancestors".

records.source: כִּֽי־תְמ֣וֹל אֲ֭נַחְנוּ וְלֹ֣א נֵדָ֑ע כִּ֤י צֵ֖ל יָמֵ֣ינוּ עֲלֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: For yesterday [are] we and do not know, for a shadow [are] our days on earth.
pieces: For we were born only yesterday and know nothing; \q our days on earth are a shadow.

L.9: For we [are of] yesterday and do not know, \q for our days on earth [are] a shadow.

R.9: We have hardly been here any time at all, and we know nothing. \q Our lives on earth pass like a shadow.

decisions.choice: we are yesterday: our life is new and short
decisions.reason: "We are yesterday" means we were born only a short time ago. Bildad compares his own generation with the long wisdom of the ancestors.

decisions.choice: a shadow: something that passes quickly
decisions.reason: A shadow lengthens and is gone (14:2; Psalm 144:4; 1 Chronicles 29:15). The line echoes Job's own laments about the shortness of life (7:6-7).

decisions.choice: we do not know: we know nothing
decisions.reason: The verb has no object: our own knowledge is small compared with that of the ages.

decisions.choice: born only yesterday
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the picture means (m1); Literal keeps it.

records.source: הֲלֹא־הֵ֣ם י֭וֹרוּךָ יֹ֣אמְרוּ לָ֑ךְ וּ֝מִלִּבָּ֗ם יוֹצִ֥אוּ מִלִּֽים׃
records.gloss: Will they not teach you, say to you, and from their heart bring out words?
pieces: Will they not teach you and tell you, \q bringing out words from their understanding?

L.10: Will they not teach you [and] speak to you, \q and bring out words from their heart?

R.10: They will teach you and tell you \q words that come from real understanding.

decisions.choice: heart: mind, understanding
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is where a person thinks and understands. The ancestors' words come from understanding, unlike the wind of Job's words (8:2).

decisions.choice: a question that expects yes
decisions.reason: "Will they not ...?" means "Surely they will".

decisions.choice: they: the former generations
decisions.reason: The pronoun "they" is written out, which makes it emphatic: they, not we who were born yesterday (8:9).

decisions.choice: a statement in place of the question
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer the question expects (m2).

records.source: הֲיִֽגְאֶה־גֹּ֭מֶא בְּלֹ֣א בִצָּ֑ה יִשְׂגֶּה־אָ֥חוּ בְלִי־מָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: Does papyrus grow tall without a marsh? Does reed grow without water?
pieces: Can papyrus grow tall where there is no marsh? \q Can reeds flourish without water?

L.11: Can papyrus grow tall without a marsh? \q Can reeds grow without water?

R.11: Can papyrus plants grow tall without a swamp? \q Can reeds grow without water?

decisions.choice: papyrus and reeds: plants that grow in water
decisions.reason: Papyrus (gome') is the tall marsh plant of the Nile from which Moses' basket was made (Exodus 2:3; Isaiah 18:2). The reed or marsh grass ('achu) grew where the cows of Pharaoh's dream fed by the river (Genesis 41:2). Both die quickly without water.

decisions.choice: a proverb-like question that begins a picture
decisions.reason: Bildad now gives the kind of saying the ancestors taught (8:8-10). The picture runs to verse 13, which applies it: a plant cut off from water withers, and so does one who forgets God.

decisions.choice: grow tall: rise up
decisions.reason: The verb (ga'ah) means to rise high; it can also mean to be proud, which fits the godless of verse 13.

decisions.choice: papyrus plants
decisions.reason: Readable adds "plants" so the reader knows papyrus is a plant here, not paper.

records.source: עֹדֶ֣נּוּ בְ֭אִבּוֹ לֹ֣א יִקָּטֵ֑ף וְלִפְנֵ֖י כָל־חָצִ֣יר יִיבָֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: Still it [is] in its greenness, not cut off, and before any grass it dries up.
pieces: While it is still in flower and not yet cut, \q it withers sooner than any other plant.

L.12: While it [is] still in its green shoots [and] not cut down, \q it dries up before any [other] grass.

R.12: Even while it is still green and no one has cut it, \q it dries up faster than any other plant.

decisions.choice: its greenness: its fresh growth
decisions.reason: The word ('ev) means a green shoot or bud (Song of Songs 6:11). The plant is young and fresh, not yet ripe for cutting.

decisions.choice: before any grass: sooner than other plants
decisions.reason: "Before any grass" means ahead of the grass around it: the water plant, once its water is gone, withers first.

decisions.choice: not cut off: no one has harvested it
decisions.reason: The verb (qataf) is used for plucking or cutting (Deuteronomy 23:26). The plant dies of itself, without anyone cutting it down.

decisions.choice: [other] grass / any other plant
decisions.reason: English needs "other" to show the comparison (m2); Literal brackets it.

records.source: כֵּ֗ן אָ֭רְחוֹת כָּל־שֹׁ֣כְחֵי אֵ֑ל וְתִקְוַ֖ת חָנֵ֣ף תֹּאבֵֽד׃
records.gloss: So [are] [the] paths of all who forget God, and [the] hope of [the] godless will perish.
pieces: Such is the end of all who forget God; \q the hope of the godless will perish.

L.13: So [are] the paths of all who forget God, \q and the hope of the godless will perish.

R.13: That is what happens to everyone who forgets God. \q The hope of godless people will come to nothing.

decisions.choice: paths: the course of a life and where it leads
decisions.reason: The paths ('orchot) of a person are the way they live and the end it brings (Proverbs 1:19). The old Greek translation reads "the end" here, which may reflect a slightly different Hebrew word; the sense is close.

decisions.choice: the godless: one who has turned from God
decisions.reason: The word (chanef) means one who is profane, who has no regard for God (15:34; 20:5; 27:8). It stands parallel to "all who forget God".

decisions.choice: so: the picture applied
decisions.reason: "So" applies the picture of verses 11-12: as the reed without water, so the person cut off from God.

decisions.choice: hope: Job's word
decisions.reason: Hope (tiqwah) is the word Job used of his days ending "without hope" (7:6). Bildad's reply implies a reason: the hope of the godless perishes.

decisions.choice: the end
decisions.reason: Balanced says where the paths lead (m1); Literal keeps "paths".

records.source: אֲשֶׁר־יָק֥וֹט כִּסְל֑וֹ וּבֵ֥ית עַ֝כָּבִ֗ישׁ מִבְטַחֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Whose confidence snaps, and a spider's house [is] his trust.
pieces: What they rely on snaps like a thread; \q what they trust in is a spider's web.

L.14: whose confidence snaps, \q and whose trust [is] a spider's house.

R.14: What they count on will break apart. \q What they trust in is as weak as a spider's web.

decisions.choice: snaps: is cut off
decisions.reason: The word (yaqot) is rare and its meaning is uncertain. It may be a verb meaning to be cut off or break, or a noun meaning fine threads. Next to the spider's web either way it pictures something thin and easily broken.

decisions.choice: a spider's house: a web
decisions.reason: A spider's house is its web, which cannot bear any weight (Isaiah 59:5-6). That is all the godless have to lean on.

decisions.choice: confidence and trust: what a person relies on
decisions.reason: Confidence (kesel) and trust (mivtach) both mean the thing a person relies on for safety.

decisions.choice: like a thread
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "like a thread" to hold together the two possible senses of the rare word (m1) with the web of the next line.

decisions.choice: they ... their
decisions.reason: The Hebrew singular means any godless person (8:13). Balanced and Readable use "they", which keeps the general sense; Literal follows the Hebrew.

records.source: יִשָּׁעֵ֣ן עַל־בֵּ֭יתוֹ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲמֹ֑ד יַחֲזִ֥יק בּ֝֗וֹ וְלֹ֣א יָקֽוּם׃
records.gloss: He leans on his house, and it does not stand; he takes hold of it, and it does not endure.
pieces: They lean on their house, but it will not stand; \q they cling to it, but it will not hold.

L.15: He leans on his house, and it does not stand; \q he takes hold of it, and it does not hold.

R.15: They lean on their web, but it does not hold them up. \q They grab hold of it, but it gives way.

decisions.choice: his house: the spider's web, and the godless person's household
decisions.reason: "His house" carries on the spider's house of verse 14, and also points to the godless person's own house and family, which cannot hold him up. Bildad's words cut close to Job, whose house fell (1:19).

decisions.choice: he leans, he takes hold: the same picture twice
decisions.reason: The two lines say the same thing, as Hebrew poetry often does: whatever he grips gives way.

decisions.choice: endure: remain standing
decisions.reason: The verb (qum) means to rise or stand; here, to stay up, to last.

decisions.choice: their web
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the spider's web of verse 14 so the picture is clear (m1).

records.source: רָטֹ֣ב ה֭וּאלִפְנֵי־שָׁ֑מֶשׁ וְעַ֥ל גַּ֝נָּת֗וֹ יֹֽנַקְתּ֥וֹתֵצֵֽא׃
records.gloss: A well-watered [plant] he [is] before [the] sun, and over his garden his shoots go out.
pieces: They are like a lush plant in the sunshine, \q sending out shoots all over the garden.

L.16: He [is] a lush [plant] before the sun, \q and over his garden his shoots spread out.

R.16: Such a person is like a healthy plant growing in the sun, \q its new shoots spreading all over the garden.

decisions.choice: he: the godless person, pictured as a plant
decisions.reason: Verses 16-19 give a second plant picture. Most likely it continues the picture of the godless: a plant that flourishes for a time and is then torn up and forgotten (8:18), so that others grow in its place (8:19). Some read it as a contrast: a well-rooted plant that survives being uprooted and grows again, like the blameless person of 8:20. The words allow both.

decisions.choice: lush: full of sap
decisions.reason: The word (ratov) means moist, full of sap (24:8 uses the verb of being wet). The plant is green and healthy.

decisions.choice: before the sun: in the sunshine
decisions.reason: "Before the sun" means in the full light of the sun, flourishing for all to see.

decisions.choice: like a lush plant
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "like" because the person is compared with a plant; Literal follows the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: Such a person
decisions.reason: Readable names who is meant, as Bildad's picture shifts from a plant to a person and back.

records.source: עַל־גַּ֭ל שָֽׁרָשָׁ֣יו יְסֻבָּ֑כוּ בֵּ֖ית אֲבָנִ֣ים יֶחֱזֶֽה׃
records.gloss: Over a heap his roots are wrapped; between stones he looks.
pieces: Their roots twine around a pile of rocks; \q they look for a hold among the stones.

L.17: Over a heap his roots are wrapped; \q he looks for [a place] among the stones.

R.17: Its roots wrap around a heap of rocks \q and push their way in among the stones.

decisions.choice: a heap: a pile of stones
decisions.reason: The word (gal) usually means a heap of stones (Genesis 31:46); in Song of Songs 4:12 a similar word means a spring. A pile of stones fits "stones" in the next line.

decisions.choice: he looks: he seeks a place among the stones
decisions.reason: The verb (chazah) means to see or look. Its sense here is unclear: the plant may "look upon" or search out the stones for a place to root. Some suggest a slightly different Hebrew word meaning "take hold"; the old Greek translation has "live". The picture is of roots that grip the rocks.

decisions.choice: between stones
decisions.reason: The word (beit) can mean "house" or "between". With "stones" it is most likely "among the stones", though "a house of stones" (a wall) is possible.

decisions.choice: look for a hold / push their way in
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the plant is doing in the picture (m2).

records.source: אִם־יְבַלְּעֶ֥נּוּ מִמְּקוֹמ֑וֹ וְכִ֥חֶשׁ בּ֝֗וֹ לֹ֣א רְאִיתִֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: If one swallows him from his place, then it will deny him: I have not seen you.
pieces: But when they are torn from their place, \q it disowns them: "I never saw you."

L.18: If [one] swallows him up from his place, \q then it will deny him: "I have not seen you."

R.18: But when it is pulled up from its place, \q that place disowns it and says, "I never saw you."

decisions.choice: swallow up: destroy, uproot
decisions.reason: To swallow up (bala') means to destroy completely (2:3; 10:8). Here the plant is torn out of the ground.

decisions.choice: one swallows him: an impersonal subject
decisions.reason: No subject is named. It may be God, or simply "if he is torn up". Either way the plant is removed.

decisions.choice: his place denies him: no trace remains
decisions.reason: The place where the plant grew says it never knew it. Job had said the same of the dead: "his place will not know him again" (7:10; compare Psalm 103:16). Bildad applies Job's words to the godless.

decisions.choice: torn / pulled up
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture means for a plant (m1).

records.source: הֶן־ה֭וּא מְשׂ֣וֹשׂ דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וּ֝מֵעָפָ֗ר אַחֵ֥ר יִצְמָֽחוּ׃
records.gloss: Look, this [is] the joy of his way, and from the dust another will sprout.
pieces: See, that is the joy of their way, \q and from the soil others will spring up.

L.19: Look, this [is] the joy of his way, \q and from the dust others will sprout.

R.19: That is all the joy such a life brings! \q Then other plants spring up from the same soil.

decisions.choice: the joy of his way: said in bitter irony
decisions.reason: Read with 8:16-18 as a picture of the godless, "the joy of his way" is ironic: this is all his joy comes to. If 8:16-19 is read as a contrast (see 8:16), the line means the plant still rejoices on its way, and new shoots spring up from the ground.

decisions.choice: from the dust others: others take its place
decisions.reason: "Another" (singular with a plural verb) means other plants. The godless person is replaced and forgotten.

decisions.choice: look: calling attention
decisions.reason: The word (hen) points to what follows: "see", "there it is".

decisions.choice: an exclamation
alternatives: Look, this is the joy of his way
decisions.reason: Readable puts the irony (m1) into an exclamation.

records.source: הֶן־אֵ֭ל לֹ֣א יִמְאַס־תָּ֑ם וְלֹֽא־יַ֝חֲזִ֗יק בְּיַד־מְרֵעִֽים׃
records.gloss: Look, God will not reject a blameless [person], and he will not take hold of [the] hand of evildoers.
pieces: Surely God does not reject anyone who is blameless, \q nor does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} take evildoers by the hand.

L.20: Look, God does not reject a blameless [person], \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not take hold of the hand of evildoers.

R.20: God will never turn away from a person who is blameless, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} never helps those who do evil.

decisions.choice: blameless: the word used of Job in 1:1
decisions.reason: "Blameless" (tam) is the book's word for Job (1:1, 8; 2:3; 9:20-22). Bildad states the rule that Job's case puts to the test: God does not reject the blameless.

decisions.choice: reject: the verb Job used in 7:16
decisions.reason: The verb (ma'as) is the one Job used when he said "I loathe my life" (7:16). Bildad says God does not reject the blameless; Job feels rejected (10:3).

decisions.choice: take hold of the hand: support, help
decisions.reason: To take someone by the hand is to support and strengthen them (Isaiah 41:13; 42:6).

decisions.choice: never helps
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means (m3).

records.source: עַד־יְמַלֵּ֣ה שְׂח֣וֹק פִּ֑יךָ וּשְׂפָתֶ֥יךָ תְרוּעָֽה׃
records.gloss: Until he will fill your mouth [with] laughter, and your lips [with] a shout of joy.
pieces: He will yet fill your mouth with laughter \q and your lips with shouts of joy.

L.21: Yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will fill your mouth [with] laughter, \q and your lips [with] shouts of joy.

R.21: God will again fill your mouth with laughter, \q and you will shout for joy.

decisions.choice: until: yet, still
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads 'ad, "until". Many read the same consonants as 'od, "still, yet", which only changes a vowel. Read as "until", it links to verse 20: God will not reject the blameless until he fills his mouth with laughter. Either way, Bildad promises Job joy again.

decisions.choice: a shout of joy: a loud cry of gladness
decisions.reason: The word (teru'ah) is a loud shout or trumpet blast, used for the shout of joy at a festival or victory (1 Samuel 4:5; Psalm 33:3).

decisions.choice: your lips: the verb fill carries over
decisions.reason: The second line has no verb of its own; "fill" serves both.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God, the subject of the verb.

records.source: שֹׂנְאֶ֥יךָ יִלְבְּשׁוּ־בֹ֑שֶׁת וְאֹ֖הֶל רְשָׁעִ֣ים אֵינֶֽנּוּ׃פ
records.gloss: Those who hate you will be clothed [with] shame, and [the] tent of wicked [people] will not be.
pieces: Those who hate you will be clothed with shame, \q and the tent of the wicked will be gone.

L.22: Those who hate you will be clothed [with] shame, \q and the tent of the wicked will be no more.

R.22: Your enemies will be covered with shame, \q and the homes of wicked people will disappear.

decisions.choice: clothed with shame: covered in disgrace
decisions.reason: Shame worn like a garment is a common picture (Psalm 35:26; 109:29; 132:18).

decisions.choice: tent: home and household
decisions.reason: The tent is the dwelling, and with it the family who live there (5:24; 18:14).

decisions.choice: will not be: Job's last words in 7:21
decisions.reason: Bildad's speech ends with the word Job used to end his: "and I will not be" (7:8, 21). Bildad says it is the wicked who will be no more, not the blameless.

decisions.choice: your enemies
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plainer word.
